newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU says 1998/99 farm set-aside may be raised.
newsitem.headline: EU says 1998/99 farm set-aside may be raised.

text.p: European Union cereals and oilseed land set aside for the 1998 harvest looks as if it will be increased, Commission officials said.
"At the moment, set-aside is more likely to go up than down," said an official, declining to talk about figures.
Last July, EU farm ministers agreed to halve the set-aside rate to five percent for the 1977 harvest.
Winter grain plantings are around four to five percent higher than a year ago, said another Commission official.
"It's horrible news," said the official, noting a record 1996 crop of 203 million tonnes.
But due to a satisfactory rate of exports, less than 10 million tonnes of grain were now expected to end up in intervention stores, against around one million tonnes at present.
At one stage, as much as 24 million tonnes was expected to land in intervention, added the second official.
Senior German agricultural officials said last week during the annual "green week" in Berlin that Germany favoured an increase in set-aside.
